row.scope_statement: The claim is limited to the Claude-coauthored automation send_webhook branch that made server-side requests to account-supplied URLs without the existing SSRF destination guard.

code_evidence.summary: Claude-assisted automation code sent server-side POST requests to account-supplied URLs without the existing SSRF destination check. The direct fix blocks private and reserved targets and redirect bounces before the request.
code_evidence.mechanism: The send_webhook branch passed cfg.url and account-controlled headers directly to fetch, which followed redirects by default. The fix applies isDeliverableUrl before the request, disables redirects, and bounds request time.

steps.title: AI change
steps.detail: The new automation action accepted a webhook URL and custom headers, then fetched the destination from the server without the existing SSRF guard.

steps.title: Security fix
steps.detail: The direct PR member validates the resolved destination, refuses redirects, and adds a ten-second timeout at the same fetch sink.

candidate_hunks.annotation: The Claude-coauthored feature added an account-configurable send_webhook action that passed cfg.url and custom headers straight to server-side fetch. With no destination check and default redirect following, an authenticated tenant could reach private, loopback, link-local, or metadata endpoints.

fix_hunks.annotation: The direct PR member routes the destination through the existing SSRF resolver guard before fetch, refuses redirect bouncing, and adds a timeout. These changes close both direct private-address requests and public-to-private redirects at the vulnerable sink.

row.scope_statement: The claim is limited to the Copilot-coauthored TypeScript Nunjucks renderer that exposed host objects to attacker-controlled templates; it does not cover the separate JavaScript-frontmatter advisory.

code_evidence.summary: Copilot-assisted TypeScript code rendered attacker-controlled Nunjucks templates with host objects and unrestricted JavaScript member access. The direct fix blocks prototype traversal and function calls and exposes only copied own data.
code_evidence.mechanism: NunjucksRenderer passed prepared inputs directly to an unrestricted Nunjucks Environment. Templates could follow constructor or prototype properties and call host functions; the fix sanitizes inputs, limits lookup to own data properties, and disables calls during rendering.

steps.title: AI change
steps.detail: The new TypeScript renderer created a default Nunjucks runtime and rendered templates against prepared host values without a sandbox boundary.

steps.title: Security fix
steps.detail: The direct PR member copies only safe own data, rejects constructor and prototype access, blocks calls, and routes the real sink through those guards.

candidate_hunks.annotation: The Copilot-coauthored TypeScript runtime created a plain Nunjucks environment and sent prepared host values directly to renderString. Attacker-controlled templates could traverse constructor and prototype properties and invoke functions in the host Node.js process.

fix_hunks.annotation: The fix replaces unrestricted JavaScript object traversal with own-data-only lookup, strips unsafe constructor and prototype keys from inputs, and blocks every template function call while Nunjucks renders. Restoring the original runtime hooks in finally confines those guards to this render operation.

The vulnerable sink previously passed prepared host values straight to the unrestricted environment. This call-site replacement makes both input sanitization and the guarded Nunjucks runtime mandatory on the actual render path.
